title: In 40 moving C. elegans, 63% of reliable pair-specific co-activity was locked to six behaviour variables; wiring and transcriptomes explained about 10% of the behaviour-independent rest
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found that the pair-specific co-activity of worm head neurons (after node effects, soma distance and homologous pairs) is very reliable, but wiring explains only 3-5% of it. What sets this reliable non-wiring part? Approach: in 40 off-food worms (Atanas 2023; 119 NeuroPAL neurons, 4,348 pairs) we divided the co-activity of each animal into a behaviour-locked part (traces predicted out of fold from velocity, reversal, head angle, head angular velocity, pumping and body curvature) and a behaviour-independent part. We measured the share of the reliable pair-specific covariance in each part and how much wiring (Cook 2019), CeNGEN transcriptome similarity, shared transmitter and lineage explain (split-half reliability calibration, leave-one-animal-out jackknife, class-label permutations). Results: the behaviour-locked part held 0.69 [0.65, 0.74] of the reliable pattern (time-shifted behaviour 0.07; 0.63 after detrending with control 0.01; velocity and reversal alone 0.59). It was low-rank (three node factors removed 80%), and similarity of neuron tuning to behaviour, measured in other animals, explained 38% of the total pattern. The behaviour-independent part was still reliable (0.69) and had more dimensions (three factors removed 53%). Wiring explained 2.6% of the total pattern and 4.0% of the behaviour-independent part. Transcriptome similarity added 5.2 points beyond wiring (permutation p = 0.004), but only 1.4 points after control for same class, ganglion and sensory/inter/motor type (p = 0.005). Lineage had no effect. The behaviour-independent coupling was concentrated in nose-tip mechanosensory (IL1, OLQ, OLL) and pharyngeal (NSM, I3) neurons. Eight on-food worms (Dag 2023) agreed in direction with wide intervals (behaviour-locked share 0.50 after detrending); the wiring increase did not replicate. Limitations: correlational; linear behaviour model with no nose-movement data; connectome and class-level transcriptome from other animals; possible cross-talk between near neurons; several controls were added after the first results.
